cards.title: Understanding Spring Boot Performance
cards.content:
Optimizing a Spring Boot application requires addressing bottlenecks across multiple layers:

  • Database I/O: Excessive queries, unindexed lookups, and unoptimized connection pooling.
  • Memory & JVM: Heap allocation, garbage collection pauses, and object churn.
  • Execution Flow: Blocking calls in high-throughput endpoints.
  • Application Startup: Heavy bean initialization and classpath scanning.

cards.title: Database Connection Pool Tuning with HikariCP
cards.content:
Spring Boot uses HikariCP as the default connection pool. Misconfigured pools can exhaust database resources or throttle application throughput.

# application.properties
spring.datasource.hikari.maximum-pool-size=20
spring.datasource.hikari.minimum-idle=10
spring.datasource.hikari.idle-timeout=300000
spring.datasource.hikari.connection-timeout=20000
spring.datasource.hikari.max-lifetime=1200000

Rule of thumb: pool_size = (core_count * 2) + effective_spindle_count.

options.text: maximum-pool-size should always be set to at least 200 regardless of database capacity
connection-timeout specifies the maximum milliseconds a caller will wait for a connection from the pool
minimum-idle must always be higher than maximum-pool-size
HikariCP requires manual registration of JDBC drivers inside @Configuration classes

cards.title: Eliminating JPA N+1 Query Problems
cards.content:
The N+1 problem occurs when fetching an entity with lazy-loaded associations triggers 1 initial query followed by N subsequent queries for related entities.

Use JOIN FETCH or @EntityGraph to load associations in a single query:

public interface OrderRepository extends JpaRepository<Order, Long> {

    @EntityGraph(attributePaths = {"customer", "items"})
    List<Order> findAllWithDetailsByStatus(OrderStatus status);
}

Also consider DTO Projections to avoid loading full entity graphs when only a few fields are needed.

cards.title: Effective Caching Strategies
cards.content:
Spring's Cache Abstraction reduces database load by keeping frequently accessed, slow-changing data in fast-access memory.

@Service
public class ProductService {

    @Cacheable(value = "products", key = "#id", unless = "#result == null")
    public ProductDTO getProduct(Long id) {
        return productRepository.findDtoById(id);
    }

    @CacheEvict(value = "products", key = "#product.id")
    public void updateProduct(Product product) {
        productRepository.save(product);
    }
}

For local in-memory caching, prefer Caffeine. For distributed topologies, integrate Redis.

pairs.right: Populates cache with method result on first invocation
Always executes the method and updates the cache
Removes one or all entries from the target cache
Triggers post-processing of caching annotations across beans

cards.title: Offloading Work with @Async and ThreadPools
cards.content:
Blocking web request threads with slow operations (such as sending emails or calling external webhooks) severely impairs throughput.

@Configuration
@EnableAsync
public class AsyncConfig {

    @Bean(name = "taskExecutor")
    public Executor taskExecutor() {
        ThreadPoolTaskExecutor executor = new ThreadPoolTaskExecutor();
        executor.setCorePoolSize(5);
        executor.setMaxPoolSize(20);
        executor.setQueueCapacity(100);
        executor.setThreadNamePrefix("AsyncWorker-");
        executor.initialize();
        return executor;
    }
}

cards.title: Startup Time Optimization & Spring AOT
cards.content:
To reduce startup latency and memory footprint:

  • Lazy Initialization: Defers bean creation until required (spring.main.lazy-initialization=true).
  • Class Data Sharing (CDS): Pre-computes class metadata into a shared archive to speed up JVM startup.
  • Spring AOT & GraalVM Native Image: Ahead-of-Time compilation translates bytecode into a standalone native binary with near-instant boot and minimal base RAM.

options.text: It permanently disables dependency injection for scoped beans
It delays potential initialization errors and adds latency to the first user request accessing the bean
It makes HTTP request handling completely non-blocking by default
It compiles Java bytecode directly into C++ binaries at build time

cards.title: Observability with Spring Boot Actuator & Micrometer
cards.content:
Performance optimization requires accurate telemetry. Actuator integrates with Micrometer to export key runtime metrics.

management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=health,metrics,prometheus
management.metrics.enable.jvm=true
management.metrics.distribution.percentiles-histogram.http.server.requests=true

Key metrics to track:

  • http.server.requests: Request rate, latency percentiles (P95, P99).
  • jvm.memory.used / jvm.gc.pause: Heap saturation and GC overhead.
  • hikaricp.connections.pending: Connection starvation indicator.
